label: 2026 Orbital Launches
delta: ~99 Falcon-family launches in 2026 as of Aug 21: a second doubleheader day saw Starlink 15-20 (SLC-4E Vandenberg, B1100 9th flight, 29 V2-Mini satellites, 0725 UTC) followed by Starlink 10-39 (SLC-40 Cape Canaveral, B1078 30th flight — the 6th booster to reach 30 flights, 1514 UTC, after an Aug 20 scrub). Coverage varied on the exact milestone number (99th-100th Falcon-family launch of 2026 depending on whether the April Falcon Heavy flight is counted separately). Previously: Starlink Group 17-50 (SLC-4E Vandenberg, B1097 12th flight, 24 V2-Mini satellites) launched Aug 19 at 04:01 UTC, widely reported as SpaceX's 100th mission of 2026 overall (a tally that also includes Starship integrated flight tests). The Aug 15 doubleheader — Globalstar 2-R and the classified USSF-366 — launched just 38 minutes 31 seconds apart from opposite coasts, a new SpaceX record beating the prior 65-minute dual-launch mark (Aug 2024). Roughly 75% of 2026's missions have been Starlink. President Gwynne Shotwell projects ~140-145 Falcon 9 launches for the full year (2024: 138 total missions; 2025: 167). Also in this window: Starship IFT-13 flew (test flight, not counted toward this Falcon-family total) — T-0 abort July 16, successful launch July 24; IFT-14 (Booster 21 + Ship 41) remains pending, with Ship 41 completing single-engine and 6-engine static fires at Starbase's Massey Outpost Aug 19 while a NET target has reportedly slipped from Aug 28 toward early-mid September.

label: Total Booster Recoveries (All-Time)
delta: Two more landings Aug 21: OCISLY droneship touchdown (220th on that vessel) after Starlink 15-20 from Vandenberg (B1100, 9th flight), and ASOG droneship touchdown (164th on that vessel) after Starlink 10-39 from Cape Canaveral (B1078, 30th flight). 651st: OCISLY landing after the Aug 19 Starlink Group 17-50 mission from Vandenberg (B1097, 12th flight). 650th: OCISLY landing after the Aug 15 USSF-366 mission from Vandenberg (B1088, 18th flight) — the second half of a record 38.5-minute dual-launch turnaround. 649th (same day): Landing Zone 40 touchdown after the Aug 15 Globalstar 2-R mission from Cape Canaveral (B1090, 14th flight). 648th: ASOG landing after the Aug 11 Starlink 10-19 mission from Cape Canaveral (B1085, 18th flight). Note: IFT-12 Booster 19 (May 22) and IFT-13 Booster 20 (July 24) were NOT recovered — both lost during off-nominal landing-burn/splashdown attempts in Gulf of Mexico ocean landings (Starship boosters are not counted in this Falcon-family recovery tally).

label: Starlink Satellites in Orbit
delta: ~11,003 satellites in orbit (~10,987 operational) as of Aug 21, 2026, out of 12,769 ever launched (1,766 decayed), per KeepTrack — following the Aug 21 Starlink 15-20 and 10-39 launches (29 + 29 V2-Mini sats). Previously: ~10,979 in orbit as of the Aug 19 Starlink Group 17-50 launch, which pushed the constellation past the 11,000-satellite mark for the first time. SpaceX filed an FCC application July 6 for up to 100,000 Gen3 satellites across two new VLEO shells with W-/D-band frequencies, positioned as AI-data-center backhaul infrastructure in addition to consumer broadband. Aug 4 Q2 earnings: Starlink generated $4.3B of SpaceX's $7.81B quarterly revenue (55% of total).

label: Starlink Subscribers
delta: 12M subscribers per Q2 2026 earnings (Aug 4), up 66% YoY. Starlink revenue $4.3B in Q2 2026 (55% of SpaceX's total). Previously: 10.3M subscribers confirmed in the May 20, 2026 S-1 filing (doubled YoY); Starlink segment profit $1.2B in Q1 2026. 160+ countries served. ARPU: $66/month Q1 2026.

label: Max Single Booster Reflights
delta: B1067 set a new record with its 36th flight on the Starlink 10-42 mission (July 9, 2026, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral) — the first orbital booster in history to reach 36 flights. Previously: 34th flight on Starlink 10-44 (Mar 30, 2026).

label: Starship Integrated Flight Tests
delta: IFT-14 (Booster 21 + Ship 41) update: Ship 41 completed a single-engine deorbit-burn-demonstration static fire and a full 6-engine static fire at Starbase's Massey Outpost on the night of Aug 19; Booster 21 remains in Mega Bay 1, having finished cryoproof testing July 20 and still awaiting its own static fire before rolling to Pad 2. The NET target has reportedly slipped from Aug 28 toward early-to-mid September (FAA-dependent), aiming for the first delivery of operational V3 Starlinks to full orbit and a possible first tower catch attempt of the upper stage. IFT-13 (Booster 20 V3 + Ship 40 V3) completed July 24, 2026 after a July 16 T-0 abort (6 Raptors flagged low LOX turbopump pressure from moisture; 2 engines replaced before reflight). Results: first-ever deployment of operational satellites — 20 V3 Starlink sats (6 with cameras) released in suborbit and contacted ground stations; Ship 40 relit all 3 Raptors and made a soft Indian Ocean splashdown, remaining intact afterward for the first close-up post-flight heat-shield inspection. Booster 20 was lost on its Gulf of Mexico splashdown attempt — only 10 of 13 landing-burn engines relit, 5 shut down seconds later, causing a hard impact. Prior: FAA cleared Starship to resume flights July 13, 2026, closing the IFT-12 mishap investigation (heat effects on propulsion + erroneous engine alarm settings that prevented Booster 19's reignition, May 22 loss).

label: SPCX (Nasdaq) — Post-IPO Trading
source: SEC EDGAR S-1 / CNBC / Bloomberg / Nasdaq / StockAnalysis.com
contestNote: Closed at $136.97 on Aug 22, 2026 (+2.2% from the Aug 21 close of $134.00), recovering some ground after trading as low as $132.42 intraday Aug 20, 2026 (down ~5.2% from the prior close), which extended a slide that began as a second major post-IPO lock-up tranche — about 319M restricted shares (~2.4% of shares outstanding, a potential ~20% float increase) — became eligible to trade. SPCX had closed Aug 19 at $139.65, down roughly 2.6-3%, as traders de-risked ahead of the unlock; the reaction diverges from the Aug 6 first-unlock experience, when 911.5M shares hit the float and the stock rose 6% that day and nearly 16% the next. The unlock coincided with confirmation that Starlink generated $4.3B in Q2 2026 revenue (55% of SpaceX's total) on 12M subscribers (+66% YoY), and that the Starlink constellation reached roughly 11,000 satellites in orbit. Bear-case analysts continue to flag traditional valuation models implying fair value as low as $10-30/share. Earlier: SPCX traded around $142/share intraday Aug 18 (day range $141.80-$143.00), down ~2.8-3.2% amid a broader growth-stock selloff (new US tariffs of 10-12.5% on imports from 60 countries, rising oil prices) and profit-taking ahead of the Aug 20 unlock — even after SpaceX announced a new Transporter rideshare launch contract for Vietnamese operator VinSpace's first satellites (targeted 2027). That followed a 4.45% rally to $146.23 on Aug 17 as mid-August 13F filings revealed SpaceX's largest institutional holders for the first time: Alphabet (~551.2M shares, ~$94B), Fidelity (~302.6M shares), Gigafund (~171.8M), Saudi PIF (~154.1M), Nvidia (~122.8M shares, ~$21B, via its xAI stake), and a first-time AMD position (~$565.5M); Harvard Management disclosed ~12.9M shares (~$2.2B) as its largest single U.S. equity holding. Earlier: SPCX fell 3.88% on Aug 14 — underperforming the 2.28%-down Telecommunications Services sector — as SpaceX's $60B all-stock closing of the Anysphere (Cursor) acquisition added ~391M new Class A shares to a market already digesting post-lockup supply. That interrupted a rally that had carried the stock from a 52-week low of $104.83 (Aug 3) to $146.15 intraday (Aug 13, +9.65% that day, driven by a filing showing Musk's 48.4% stake worth over $900B). Earlier in the window: Aug 6 lock-up expiration released up to 911.5M insider shares (~$100B) without triggering a sell-off (+6.1%); shares jumped 15.8% Aug 7-8 on the Q2 earnings beat and the $16.8B Terafab chip-plant confirmation; reclaimed the $135 IPO price Aug 10 (+4%); and surged 9.6% Aug 12 after Musk said AI/Grok revenue could overtake Starlink and launch revenue within 1-2 months. IPO recap: priced at $135/share June 11 (largest IPO in history, $1.77T implied valuation); all-time high $225.64 June 16; joined Nasdaq-100 July 7. Musk holds ~42-48% economic equity (filings vary by measurement date and post-Cursor dilution), ~79-85% voting control (dual-class Class B) — cannot be removed as director except by his own vote.
